title: Migrate python-multistep-service store from module dict to Store class
description: Brownfield Python migration: replace the module-level _records dict in store.py with a Store class, keeping the free-function API unchanged.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate src/store.py to use a Store class. All 6 existing tests must still pass.

  class Store:
      def __init__(self) -> None:
          self._records: dict[str, list[str]] = {}

      def save(self, key: str, values: list[str]) -> None
        — stores values under key

      def load(self, key: str) -> list[str] | None
        — returns values for key, or None if missing

      def all_keys(self) -> list[str]
        — returns list of all stored keys

      def clear(self) -> None
        — removes all records

  _store = Store()

Keep the existing free functions (save, load, all_keys, clear) as one-liners that
delegate to _store. Do not modify tests/ or any other file.
All 6 existing tests must still pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: Store class defined with save, load, all_keys, clear methods
success_criteria: uv run ruff check src/ passes
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
